findings.title: LoadOrDefault discards ErrMissing, conflating absent key with empty value
findings.whyItBreaks: Load (src/store.go:7) distinguishes a missing key (returns "", ErrMissing) from a present key whose stored value is "" (returns "", nil). LoadOrDefault (src/store.go:16) drops the error via `v, _ := Load(...)` and returns "" in both cases, so its public contract erases the presence/absence signal the store was designed to expose. Any caller that must not treat a missing value as an authoritative empty value is forced to conflate failure with real data, and the exported signature gives it no way to recover (no ok/error channel).

The new exported function therefore returns "" both when the key is absent and when the key is present with an explicitly empty string. Any caller — including out-of-repo consumers of this module — is forced to treat a missing key as a real empty value with no way to detect it, while the very existence of `ErrMissing` shows the package's contract is that absence is distinguishable. Nothing is logged and the default is not caller-specifiable, so failure is neither distinguishable nor observable.

Unlike an internal helper, the unusable contract itself is the defect and no in-repo caller is required for it to matter.

findings.title: clampPercent promises clamping but returns unclamped value
findings.whyItBreaks: The exported carrier was renamed from `toPercent` to `clampPercent`, which promises the return is capped to a 0..100 percentage. The body still computes `Math.round((done / total) * 100)` with no Math.min/Math.max, so the promise is unimplemented. The internal caller `progressBar` relies on the capped range: with `done > total`, `pct > 100`, and line 7 evaluates `"-".repeat(100 - pct)` with a negative count, which throws `RangeError: Invalid count value`. Any external consumer that trusts the name and passes out-of-range input (e.g. done=120,total=100) likewise receives 120 instead of 100.

findings.title: clampPercent does not clamp; name promises [0,100] cap it never applies
findings.whyItBreaks: The change renames the exported `toPercent` to `clampPercent`, a public carrier whose name promises the result is clamped into a 0..100 range. The body at src/progress.ts:2 is unchanged and performs no clamping (`Math.round((done / total) * 100)`), so out-of-range inputs still yield out-of-range output (e.g. done=3, total=2 -> 150; done=-1, total=4 -> -25). The only caller, `progressBar` at src/progress.ts:6, trusts the name and feeds the result straight into `"#".repeat(pct)` / `"-".repeat(100 - pct)` at src/progress.ts:7; a negative count (pct<0 or pct>100) makes `String.prototype.repeat` throw `RangeError: Invalid count value`, whereas a genuinely clamping implementation would return a valid bar. This is a public contract that ships broken: every caller is promised a bounded value the function never produces.

findings.title: recentEntries drops limit enforcement, returns all entries
findings.whyItBreaks: The base body applied `.slice(0, limit)` so at most `limit` entries were returned. The new body builds `sorted` from the full reversed array, checks only `limit <= 0`, then returns `sorted` unconditionally. The unchanged doc comment (line 1) and the exported signature promise 'Returns at most `limit` entries', so the public contract is violated: any `limit > 0` no longer caps the result. The only in-repo caller, renderFeed (src/feed.ts:8), relies on the cap — it allocates `new Array<string>(20)` and fills `i < page.length`, so with >20 inputs it now writes past index 19 and returns an array longer than the intended 20-item page (user-visible oversized feed), and every external caller trusting the doc gets an unbounded array.

findings.title: Restore `limit` cap in recentEntries; it now returns all entries
findings.whyItBreaks: The doc comment on line 1 promises "Returns at most `limit` entries, newest first", but the new body replaces `[...all].reverse().slice(0, limit)` with `return sorted` (line 5), which returns every entry whenever `limit > 0`; only the `limit <= 0` case is handled. The sole caller renderFeed (line 9) calls `recentEntries(all, 20)` and treats the result as a page of at most 20 (line 10 allocates `new Array<string>(20)`, line 11 loops `i < page.length`). With `page.length > 20` the loop writes past index 20, extending `out`, so the feed renders an unbounded number of entries instead of 20 — a user-facing regression and a broken public contract.
